cards.text: Paul's writing to the believers in Corinth, and friend, right here the letter shifts gears. He makes his appeal by the mildness and gentleness of Christ. Then he calls himself the one who is "humble when face to face with you, but bold when away."
Paul's planning a visit to Corinth. And some people there presume that he and his team live according to the flesh.

cards.question: When Paul comes to Corinth, what does he beg the Corinthians for?

answers.text: Not to need to be as bold as he expects
A warm welcome from the whole church
Some time alone with the church leaders

cards.text: Paul answers that head-on. Yes, they live in the flesh, but they're in a fight, and he wants the Corinthians to know what kind.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the weapons he and his team fight with are the weapons of the flesh.
Paul says the weapons of their warfare have divine power to demolish ___.

cards.text: No wrecking ball needed. Paul is demolishing arguments, and every presumption set up against the knowledge of God.

cards.question: Paul says they also take every thought captive. Why?

answers.text: To make it obedient to Christ
To win every debate in town

cards.text: Paul says he'll be ready to punish every act of disobedience. But first he's waiting on something from the Corinthians.

cards.question: What is Paul waiting on before he deals with every act of disobedience in Corinth?

answers.text: Titus to bring a report back
The church to pick new leaders

cards.text: Then Paul gets blunt: "You are looking at outward appearances." Friend, that's me grabbing a cookie for its sprinkles and never once checking the dough.

cards.question: Someone in Corinth is confident he belongs to Christ. True or false: Paul says he and his team belong to Christ just as much.
Paul brings up the authority the Lord gave him and his team. What does he say it's for when it comes to the Corinthians?

cards.text: Paul says even if he boasts a little too much about that authority, he won't be ashamed. And he doesn't want to seem like he's trying to frighten them by his letters.
Here's why. Some people in Corinth have been saying his letters are weighty and forceful.

cards.question: Paul's critics in Corinth say his physical presence is ___ and his speaking is of no account.

cards.text: OUCH. That's a one-star review for showing up in person, and Paul has an answer for the folks giving it.

cards.question: What's Paul's answer to the people saying his letters are strong but he's not?

answers.text: What he is in letters he'll be in person
Someone else wrote his letters for him
He'll stop writing to them altogether

cards.text: Now Paul brings up some people who commend themselves. He won't dare classify or compare himself with them.

cards.question: These people measure themselves by themselves, and Paul says that shows their ___.

cards.text: Measuring yourself by yourself? That's me judging my cookies against my own cookies, and wow, I win EVERY time! Paul won't play that game, and he won't boast beyond his limits, only within the field God assigned to him.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the field God assigned him reaches even to the Corinthians.

cards.text: Paul says he isn't overstepping his bounds when he counts Corinth in his field.

cards.question: Why isn't Paul overstepping when he counts Corinth in his field?

answers.text: His team was first to bring them the gospel
The other apostles assigned Corinth to him
He was born and raised in the city of Corinth

cards.text: Paul won't boast in other people's labors either. But he's got a hope for when the Corinthians' faith increases.

cards.question: As the Corinthians' faith increases, what does Paul hope will greatly increase too?

answers.text: His area of influence among them
The size of their gifts to him

cards.question: Why does Paul want his influence among the Corinthians to grow?

answers.text: So he can preach in the regions beyond them
So he can settle down in Corinth for good
So he can lead every church in all of Greece

cards.text: That way he's not boasting in work already done in another man's territory. Paul is NOT the coworker who presents somebody else's slides and then takes a bow.

cards.question: Paul sums it up: whoever boasts should boast in the ___.
True or false: Paul says the one who commends himself is the one who is approved.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Not to need to be as bold as he expects', is a negative clause that doesn't fit the question 'what does he beg the Corinthians for?'. The two wrong answers are noun phrases ('A warm welcome…', 'Some time alone…'). The right answer is a different kind of thing from the others and stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Stop 1 has 5 multiple choice cards (3, 8, 10, 13, 18), 2 true or false cards and 2 fill in the blank cards. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Verse 10:7 is conditional: 'If anyone is confident that he belongs to Christ…'. The card states it as a fact: 'Someone in Corinth is confident he belongs to Christ.' This drops the 'if' and adds a specific person in Corinth that the text doesn't name.

The card tells no new part of the passage. It is only a reaction joke to verse 10:10, which card 15 and card 16 already covered, plus a lead-in to card 18. It cites 10:10 but adds nothing from the text, so it doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'These people', which points back to the people introduced on story card 1. That card is no longer on screen. The question doesn't say who they are, such as 'people who commend themselves'.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'Measuring yourself by yourself?', 'That's me judging my cookies… EVERY time!' and 'Paul won't play that game, and…'. Only the opening card can have three.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
